title: Default form-url-encoded request parser materializes near-unbounded POST bodies into heap parameters
objective: Validate whether anonymous external POST requests to a default Solr core can trigger JVM OOM, GC death, restart, or sustained HTTP unavailability through form-url-encoded parser state growth.

config_changes: No Solr application/configset changes. SOLR_HEAP and Docker memory limit are validation harness safety limits. Container memory was set to 768m after an initial 512m dry run showed baseline cgroup memory near the limit, which would confound JVM heap evidence.

probe_plan.attacker_model: anonymous HTTP client against default security-off Solr Docker deployment
stop_conditions: sustained HTTP unavailability after a probe
probe_plan.success_condition: Confirmed only on OOM, GC death, restart, or sustained unavailability. Heap or latency growth alone is observed_growth_not_confirmed.

static_candidate.source: External POST application/x-www-form-urlencoded body to default core handlers such as /solr/{core}/select or /solr/{core}/query
static_candidate.sink: SolrRequestParsers.parseFormDataContent accumulates key/value bytes, optional charset buffer entries, decoded strings, and MultiMapSolrParams arrays before handler execution
static_candidate.driver: form body byte length, parameter count, key length, and value length
static_candidate.request_shape: POST /solr/{core}/select with Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded and q=*:* plus many attacker-controlled parameters in the body
static_candidate.resource_metric: target JVM heap used, GC time, parser exception/OOM, request latency
